Definition: from G2126; properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by implication, dread (concretely):--fear(-ed).
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, eulábeia is the word for fear(-ed). In Hebrews 5:7, the text says "and was heard in that he feared."
TheologicalSignificance: This word, eulábeia, does its job quietly — fear — and I leave it at that.
